newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ABARE sees flat Australian crude export earnings.
newsitem.headline: ABARE sees flat Australian crude export earnings.

text.p: Australia's export earnings from crude oil and condensate are expected to rise by only 1.5 percent to A$2 billion in 1997/98 (July-June), the Australian Bureau fo Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Tuesday.
The government's chief economic forecaster said in its June quarter bulletin that this estimate compares with forecast export earnings of 1.97 billion in 1996/97.

"In 1997/98, despite export volumes forecast to increase to 13.0 billion litres, export earnings are expected to remain at around A$2 billion. This reflects a reduction in average unit prices of around A$2 a barrel between 1996/97 and 1997/98," ABARE said.
ABARE forecast Australian crude oil and condensate production to rise by 3.8 percent to 32.6 billion litres in 1997/98 from 31.4 billion litres in 1996/97.

"Production from the Gippsland Basin in the June quarter rose by an estimated 30,000 barrels a day as a result of two new offshore platforms coming into production in Bass Strait," it said. The Bass Strait oilfields are owned by Exxon Corp and The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd.
"The flow from the Carnarvon Basin (around the coast of Western Australia) continues to rise steadily."

ABARE also revised up its trade weighted crude oil price forecast to US$18.25 a barrel in calendar 1997, down nine percent on 1996 due to increased supply. The price is expected to continue to rise to US$19.50 in 1998.

Liquified natural gas (LNG) export volumes are expected to increase slightly to 7.6 million tonnes in 1997/98, with the full output capacity of the industry either under contract or finding ready markets.
ABARE said LNG exports are estimated to rise by A$170 million to A$1.54 billion in 1996/97 and to ease to A$1.5 billion in 1997/98 due to lower oil prices.
